answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network binds agent communication to staked topological cut verifications and multi-agent auditing. Graph cuts require verifiers to deposit stake, meaning an attacker cannot merely echo fake identities across clustered nodes. Instead of transmitting hollow noise, each node must prove state authenticity by verifying a structured cryptographic sonnet exchanged over disjoint routes. Staking physical-tier copper token bonds ensures dishonest collusions face deterministic slashing, forcing superlinear attacker cost scaling with graph partition size.
